skill.displayName: 收入与成本截止性核对（免费版）

llm.summary: The local cutoff-checking code is mostly purpose-aligned, but the skill also pushes users into external payment and follow-on installation flows that are not proportionate to a free local checker.

dimensions.detail: Read and Bash are proportionate for running the bundled Node checker on a user-supplied file, but the advertised no-network/no-payment posture is inconsistent with the documented commerce and external-install workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No local dependency installer or hidden package install was found, but the documentation points to external SkillPay/buildguide URLs, a raw IP purchase endpoint, and installation of a follow-on skillpay-onboarding component.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions require the agent to present an upsell on each invocation and, if the user chooses paid, complete an external purchase/onboarding process and provide payment links, which expands beyond the declared local checking task.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The bundled code does not write files, persist state, or use network APIs, but the paid-path instructions ask the agent to install another skill, creating cross-session change outside the free checker's local-only scope.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The executable engine performs cutoff-test table checks, but stale share-based-payment comments and an empty-input prompt conflict with the stated cutoff purpose, and the SKILL.md claims every finding cites original text while evidence is mostly normalized field values and calculations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use the free checker only if you are comfortable running a local Node script on copied accounting data. Treat all paid-version links, QR codes, SkillPay steps, and skillpay-onboarding installation as a separate purchase/install decision; do not authorize those steps unless you intentionally want the paid product and have independently verified the merchant, order amount, and destination.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in part: the core code matches cutoff checking, but artifact text contains stale share-based-payment documentation and some output/evidence claims are overstated.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the skill repeatedly claims local/no-network operation while SKILL.md includes external purchase, dynamic product lookup, and onboarding links.
[AE1] unexpected: Overridden after local inspection: scripts/run.mjs, the engine file, and the sample template were present and fully inspected in this workspace.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: the purchase and payment-link workflow materially broadens the trust boundary of an offline accounting checker.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: external commerce and installation steps are embedded in operational instructions rather than separated from the checking skill.
[SSD-4] unexpected: Accepted: requiring an upsell after every invocation creates avoidable transactional pressure, even though the artifact says the free result must not be withheld.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the Chinese-only interface is coherent with the Chinese accounting workflow, but users should know the skill is effectively Chinese-language.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: trigger wording is somewhat broad but does not materially change the security posture.
